raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add native Rust GLM5Next chat rendering for GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash through `--tokenizer-mode glm5_next`, supporting both model templates, tool calls, reasoning options, and multimodal content.

## Claims

- Support both GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash with native Rust rendering.
- Compared with the HF MiniJinja backend, text/tool rendering throughput reaches:
  - **1.50x** for short tool conversations.
  - **1.75–1.79x** for parallel tool calls.
  - **1.77–1.86x** for long tool histories.

## Validation

- Targeted GLM5Next tests: **14 passed, 1 ignored**. The ignored video decoding test requires FFmpeg and ffprobe.

  ```bash
  cd rust
  cargo test -p vllm-chat glm5_next --lib
  ```

- Benchmarked both model templates against the HF MiniJinja backend using identical requests, **4 server CPU cores**, and **concurrency 64**. Results above use two 4-second runs per configuration.
- Online validation covered image requests, multiple images, streaming responses, and tool calls with images.
- Multimodal token sequences and pixel tensors matched Transformers in the tested reference cases.

## Details

Replace template interpretation with model-specific Rust rendering while reusing existing tokenization and engine integration. Implement GLM5Next image and video preprocessing according to Transformers behavior.

Performance measurements cover frontend rendering and tokenization, excluding model inference. Video preprocessing retains vLLM's existing 30,000-token budget.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [ ] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [ ] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [ ] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

   **GLM-5.3** is the newest model in the GLM-5 series — a ~743B-parameter MoE (39B active) from **Z-AI**.
-  Architecture and serving flags are identical to GLM-5.2; the packaging change is that the

+  The **default `zai-org/GLM-5.3` checkpoint is native FP8** — BF16 weights live under the suffixed `zai-org/GLM-5.3-BF16` repo.
 
   The FP8 checkpoint fits on a single 8xH200 / 8xH20 node and — with FP8 KV cache — reaches the full 1M-token context on 8xB200.
   An NVFP4 checkpoint for Blackwell is published by Inferact (`Inferact/GLM-5.3-NVFP4`).
 
   ## Prerequisites
 
-  - **vLLM 0.28.0** or newer.
+  - **vLLM:** a build containing [native GLM5Next support (#62424)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62424), including the matching Rust frontend binary.
+  - **Transformers:** 5.15.0 or newer.
   - **GPU:** 8xH200 or 8xH20 (141 GB each) for single-node FP8; 8xB200 (180 GB each) for the full 1M context.
 
   ## Installation
 
-  ```bash
-  uv venv
-  source .venv/bin/activate
-  uv pip install "vllm==0.28.0" --torch-backend=auto
-  uv pip install "transformers>=5.15.0"
-  ```
+  Use a wheel or container built with #62424 for the Rust commands below.
+  The older release and hardware-specific image pins record prior model validation;
+  they need an updated build to use `--tokenizer-mode glm5_next`.
+
+  ## Frontends

+  The command builder defaults to **Rust** and adds `--tokenizer-mode glm5_next`.
+  With `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, this selects native GLM5Next chat rendering for
+  GLM-5.3, including tool calls and reasoning options.
+
+  Select **Python** in the command builder, or set `VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0`,
+  to use the Hugging Face renderer on the same build. On older builds that do not
+  recognize `glm5_next`, also replace `--tokenizer-mode glm5_next` with
+  `--tokenizer-mode auto`.

-  vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 \
+  VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 \
